AgentDiagnostic.description: One bounded diagnostic produced while resolving an Agent context.

AgentProfileIdentity.description: Stable, content-free identity safe for events, reports, and diagnostics.

AgentSource.description:
Where an Agent package came from. Source determines trust; a package
cannot declare its own.

ArtifactId.description:
Opaque durable artifact identity.

Opaque on purpose: it is generated locally from validated bytes, so a
remote filename or URI can never steer where a payload is written or read.

ArtifactTrust.description:
How much the local runtime trusts an artifact's origin. Always
`Untrusted` for anything a remote server produced.

ArtifactValidation.description: Outcome of validating a claim against the retained bytes.

AssistantTurn.description: Normalized assistant result consumed by Core and Runtime.

ContentBlock.description:
Provider-neutral content in an assistant or tool result.

Rich content is deliberately a bounded reference.  The model layer does
not fetch a URI or persist a remote payload as part of request projection.

oneOf.description:
A locally verified raster image, carried as base64.

The bytes come from the product attachment store, which has already
sniffed the type and hashed the payload, so `mime_type` is the
server-verified value and never a client claim. The base64 `data` is
bounded by [`MAX_CONTENT_BYTES`] like every other content, which is
what makes an oversized image a labelled degradation at the injection
site instead of a provider-side rejection mid-run.

ContentBlockMeta.description:
Shared per-block facts. Every block records its position, what the remote
claimed, and whether the retained form is complete.

audience.description:
Validated audience annotation. Advisory only: it never changes who may
read a block, only how a UI may present it.

ordinal.description:
Position in the tool's original result, preserved even when a block is
truncated or promoted to an artifact.

truncated.description: True when the retained inline form is shorter than what the tool sent.

agent.description:
Optional fully qualified Agent selector (`builtin:legacy` or
`workspace:<id>`). Workspace sources still require Project Trust.

oneOf.description:
Optional server-owned product session. When present, the server resolves
its exact runtime run binding; product callers must not use `latest`.

workspace_activation.description: Whether repository-owned project config and MCP activation were enabled.

CreateJobWorkspace.description:
Per-job workspace binding for create-job.

- `task`: isolated workspace under `base`/`name` (existing behavior).
- `folder` / `repo`: bind tools/state to an absolute local `root`.
  The opened path is the real execution root (not the API process cwd).

base.description:
Task base directory (`kind = task` only). Defaults to
`<server state_dir>/tasks` when omitted.

fork_at_run_id.description:
The already-final parent run to branch from. The server derives the
terminal event sequence and rejects anything incomplete or corrupt.

idempotency_key.description:
Required client-generated key. Retrying the exact same action returns
the same child; a body mismatch returns a typed conflict.

truncate_after_message_seq.description:
Edit-and-resend: the parent message-ledger sequence of the user message
being replaced. The child is seeded with the parent history up to that
message and continues from the text the client sends as the child's
first message; the parent session, its trace, and its transcript are
untouched. The value must be a positive sequence already recorded in
the parent's message ledger for `fork_at_run_id`.

attachments.description:
Additive. An old client omits it and keeps working; a new client that
sends it to an old server is refused by `deny_unknown_fields` rather than
silently ignored, which is the rule this field deliberately inherits.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the HTML entry file (e.g. `dist/index.html`).

CreateProductReviewRequest.description:
Request accepted by the HTTP surface. The server captures and validates
the target before constructing the internal ProductStore record.

EvaluatorMode.description: Whether semantic plan ambiguity may invoke the model evaluator.

ExecutionBudgetExhaustion.description:
Typed budget refusal emitted before new work begins, or immediately after
an indivisible model response crosses a token/cost boundary.

ExecutionBudgetLimits.description:
Independent limits for the lifecycle phases and their observable work.
`None` means that this phase has not resolved that dimension yet.

max_cost_microunits.description: Cost enforcement is deferred until provider price metadata exists.

ExecutionBudgetSnapshot.description:
Public resolved budget snapshot used by events, checkpoints, state, API,
reports, and UIs.

cost_enforced.description:
Cost is enforceable only when priced usage has been supplied. Generic
provider clients expose zero here rather than claiming enforcement.

ExecutionBudgetUsage.description: Counters consumed by an execution policy.

ExecutionDegradation.description:
Explicit, safe degradation fact. Fallbacks are never silent and do not
change permissions or erase previously recorded evidence.

workspace_digest.description:
A stable redacted identity. The canonical local path is never persisted
in this structure or in resume diagnostics.

ExecutionPhase.description:
Lifecycle phases used in budget and degradation facts. These values are
safe diagnostics; they do not contain model reasoning.

ExternalEffect.description:
An effect outside the workspace that a tool reported causing.

Recorded so a Finalizer never claims an unverified external action
succeeded, and so an indeterminate outcome stays visible.

indeterminate.description: True when it is unknown whether the effect happened.

kind.description: What kind of effect, for example `mcp_tool_call` or `network_write`.

target.description: Display-safe target description. Never a credential-bearing URL.

FinalOutcomeStatus.description:
User-visible terminal classification. This is deliberately separate from
process-level `RunStatus` and compatibility `TerminationReason`.

FinalizationRecord.description:
Durable finalization record. The output is bounded before persistence by
the Finalizer and contains only user-visible synthesis, never hidden model
reasoning.

FinalizerPolicy.description: How the independent run finalizer is allowed to synthesize the user answer.

InternalCallId.description: Stable Rove identity for a tool invocation.

answer_aborted.description:
Additive R2b projection of `events`: `true` only when this run's
assistant answer was stopped by the user after it had already published
text, so the text is a salvaged partial rather than a complete response.

The field is omitted when it does not apply. A `true` value is always
conclusive; the omission is conclusive only for a settled listing, which
requires both of these:

* `status` is terminal (`done`, `error`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`).
  A run still in flight lists only the events published so far, and its
  salvage message is published when the stopped turn settles — up to the
  runtime's abort-salvage window after the stop — while `status` changes
  only on the terminal event. An in-flight response can therefore omit
  this field for a run that is about to keep a partial.
* `events` is contiguous: its `seq` values run `1..=n` with no gap. A
  persisted response is projected from the run index rather than from
  `trace.jsonl`, so a gap there means the listing is not the run's whole
  event list; the transcript endpoint reports that case explicitly
  instead (`partial`, `missing_event_range`).

Within those bounds the omission separates a complete answer
(`aborted: false` on its `llm_message`), a turn that failed
(`status: "error"`, no `llm_message`), and a stop that produced nothing
(a `cancelled` run with no `llm_message`). All three still serialize
exactly as they did before this field existed. A run resumed from
`resumed_from_run_id` reports only its own events; the session-wide view
is the transcript, whose segments project each bound run in turn.

OnboardProductProviderRequest.description:
The HTTP-visible onboarding body — the only Product payload that carries a
secret. The credential is accepted transiently, handed straight to the OS
keyring by the shared onboarding service, and never read back, logged, or
serialized into any response. `write_only` marks it in the spec so generated
clients know it is not returned.

credential.description: The raw provider key. Bounded, never persisted outside the OS keyring.

oneOf.description: Reuse an existing catalog profile id to rotate or repair its credential.

PlanDecision.description: Rule-first decision made after a terminal step record.

PlanDecisionRecord.description:
Persisted correlation between one terminal step fact and its rule-first
plan decision.

PlanIdentity.description:
Stable identity for one logical plan and one immutable-compatible
revision.  The current runtime uses the identity to correlate the
append-only step ledger while retaining the legacy `TaskPlan` wire shape.

PlanRevision.description: An immutable revision of the remaining plan.

ProcedureApplication.description:
Bounded procedure material supplied to one execution boundary.

`hydration_hash` identifies the exact section projection admitted to the
model. The source body remains pinned by `reference.content_hash` and the
Agent profile snapshot.

ProcedureCapabilityBinding.description:
One concrete tool binding visible to a procedure at a run/step boundary.
A binding describes availability and policy; it never grants permission.

ProcedureDeviation.description:
Safe, persisted deviation fact. It can inform evaluation, but cannot
weaken approval, schema, workspace, or capability enforcement.

ProcedureDeviationReason.description: Typed reason why execution departed from selected procedure guidance.

ProcedureReference.description: An audit-grade pointer to a procedure, safe to persist and to show.

ProcedureTrust.description:
How much authority a procedure source carries.

Ordered most to least trusted, so `Ord` can be used for policy comparisons.

selector.description:
Configured base selector. A request may still provide an explicit
selector, and the resolved run identity is emitted canonically.

ProductAttachmentAvailability.description:
Why an attachment payload cannot be served, mirroring the durable-record
status. Deliberately separate from [`ProductArtifactAvailability`]: its
`cleaned`/`too_large` words carry artifact-specific meanings that an
attachment does not have.

ProductAttachmentId.description: Server-owned identity for one session-scoped attachment record. Generated by the server from a fresh ULID; never derived from a client name, path, or content.

ProductAttachmentStatus.description:
The row lifecycle. `staged` is written-but-unreferenced, `referenced` is
durable session content with no TTL, and `expired` was deliberately
reclaimed — a visible conflict rather than a silent 404.

ProductAttachmentUploadResponse.description:
The `201` body. Every field is server-verified: `content_type`, `size`, and
`sha256` come from the bytes this server hashed, and `warnings` is the
stored `scan_flags`.

content_type.description: The locally verified type. The client's claim is never echoed.

warnings.description:
Always present, and always an array, so a client can distinguish "no
warnings" from "this server did not tell me".

ProductAuthorizationOutcome.description:
The terminal tool event one decided call reached, when the run's event
log records one. Payload is deliberately not projected here; the artifact
and transcript surfaces already carry it.

decided_via.description:
Which surface recorded the decision (`job_api`, `job_cancel`,
`job_responder_lost`); `null` when no decision surface was recorded
(still pending, interrupted at startup, or pre-schema-v5 rows).

updated_at.description: Last durable update; for decided rows this is the decision time.

truncated.description:
True when the limit cut the page; there is no cursor because the
panel only claims to show recent history.

ProductControlId.description: Server-owned identity for one steer or follow-up control message.

ProductEvent.description:
One product-level directory fact.

`seq` is the durable, strictly increasing event order and doubles as the SSE
`id:` field, so a reconnecting client resumes exactly where it stopped.
`summary` is a bounded, secret-free JSON object of status/outcome fields
only: message content, tool arguments, error details, and secrets never
appear there.

type.description:
Serialized as `type`, the canonical stream-event discriminator, so the
frame body uses the same field name as the job SSE envelope.

ProductEventKind.description:
Product-level directory event kinds.

The serialized value is a dotted namespace (`domain.fact`) rather than the
`snake_case` used by the other product enums, because the same value is the
SSE `event:` name of `GET /product/events`, so it is part of the endpoint's
wire contract rather than an internal label.

ProductFork.description:
Immutable source boundary for one child product session. This contains
runtime identities and references only; canonical event facts continue to
live in the source workspace StateStore.

oneOf.description:
The message that sequence identifies. Recorded alongside the sequence so
the child's seed can be cut even after the parent's message ledger is
gone (a parent catalog row may be deleted while its runtime artifacts
stay readable).

truncate_after_message_seq.description:
Set when the child was built by editing one of the parent's messages:
the ledger sequence of the user message the child's seed stops before.
Absent on a plain terminal-boundary fork, which keeps the whole prefix.

ProductForkId.description: Server-owned identity for immutable product-session fork provenance.

transport_deprecated.description:
Server-owned deprecation verdict for this server's transport, so the
client renders one truth instead of hardcoding which name is legacy.

attachments.description:
Attachments this message references, in the order the client sent them.

Additive: an empty set is omitted from the payload, so a message with no
attachments serialises byte-identically to what it did before this field
existed, and a pre-migration payload deserialises with an empty set.

queue_order.description:
Explicit successor-queue position, written by a reorder or a
`successor` promotion. `None` means the message has never been moved and
keeps its `seq` (creation) order; clients sort the queue by
`queue_order ?? seq`. The field is additive, so a pre-migration payload
parses unchanged.

ProductMessageAttachmentRef.description:
One attachment reference on a durable message, projected for the client.

`content_type`, `size`, and `sha256` are the **server-verified** values taken
from the durable attachment row, never the client's claim, so a reference
cannot make the transcript report a type the bytes do not have. `name` is
display metadata and is never a path or a filename on disk.

availability.description:
Lifecycle availability. `available` is the row's own state; `expired`
means the payload was deliberately reclaimed. `missing` and `corrupt`
are reported by the paths that read the bytes — the download endpoint
and model injection — because detecting them needs a hash this
projection deliberately does not pay for.

degradation.description:
Why this reference did not reach the model even though its bytes are
fine. `None` for every reference that was projected as sent, for every
non-image reference, and for every response a pre-image client reads
(additive, omitted when absent).

ProductMessageAttachmentRequest.description:
The attachment reference a client sends with a message.

The client names an id it already uploaded and, optionally, a display name
for this reference. It cannot name a type, a size, or a path: those come from
the durable row.

ProductMessageSearchHit.description:
One message that matched, described only by the bounded excerpt around the
hit. The full body stays in the ledger; search never returns it.

message_seq.description:
Ledger sequence of the matching message, the same `seq` the message
listing and the transcript's message anchors use.

ProductMessageStatus.description:
Canonical product-facing delivery state for a user message. The legacy
control rows remain the storage representation during migration; this
projection is the only state exposed by the unified composer contract.

next_cursor.description: Token that returns the next page, absent on the last page.

ProductMigrationReceiptId.description: Server-owned identity for a committed browser migration receipt.

entry.description: Workspace-relative entry path the session was opened for.

preview_id.description: Server-owned preview session id; safe to log. Not the access token.

url.description:
Absolute loopback URL that opens the preview, embedding the session
token. Keep it out of logs, traces, and exports.

ProductPricingAvailability.description: Whether a run's cost can be computed from a trusted price snapshot.

ProductProviderOnboardingReceipt.description:
Secret-free result safe to return across the Tauri command boundary or as
an HTTP response.

ProductProviderProfileId.description:
Stable user-catalog Provider profile identity. Historical ProductStore ULIDs
remain valid because they are a subset of this bounded identifier syntax.

ProductReasoningPreference.description:
Session model configuration is explicit about the provider default. The
API never invents a reasoning level for protocols that do not support it.

ProductReviewId.description: Server-owned identity for one hard read-only Review run.

ProductReviewStatus.description:
Durable lifecycle state for a hard read-only Review. It is deliberately
separate from `ProductSessionStatus`: a Review never claims a chat turn.

ProductSearchHit.description:
One hit of a unified product search.

`session_id` is on every hit because the workspace scope answers a question
a single session cannot: which sessions contain this term. The snippet is
the only body text that leaves the API, and it is bounded and redacted by
the same builder the session-scoped search uses.

created_at.description:
The ledger timestamp of a message hit, or the trace line's own
timestamp. A legacy trace line carries none, and an invented one would
be a fabricated fact.

run_id.description: The run that owns a trace hit. Absent on a message hit.

run_ordinal.description: The binding ordinal of that run, which is also the trace reading order.

seq.description:
The hit's position inside its own corpus: the ledger `seq` of a message
hit, or the trace record's own sequence for a trace hit. Both are the
identifiers their corpus already publishes, so a client never has to
invent one.

snippet.description: Bounded excerpt around the hit, already redacted.

next_cursor.description: Token that returns the next page, absent when the search is exhausted.

scope.description: The resolved scope this page was produced for, in canonical form.

ProductSearchSource.description: Which corpus produced one search hit.

fork_point_run_id.description: Exact parent runtime run from which this session inherited history.

oneOf.description: Outcome of the most recent finished turn, absent until one finishes.

Parent product session retained as lineage even when the parent catalog
row has subsequently been deleted.

ProductSessionCompaction.description:
Bounded facts about one manual compaction of a product session.

`triggered` describes *this* call; the remaining compaction fields describe
the state the session holds afterwards. A call that produced no new summary
still reports the state it left behind, so a client can show "already
compacted", "nothing to compact", and "the breaker refuses" apart.

circuit_open.description:
Whether the session's summary model has failed to
`runtime.compaction_failure_threshold` consecutive times. Independent of
whether compaction is switched on: this is the state the automatic path
gates on, but it is not by itself a refusal — the automatic path is
refused only while `next_attempt_after` is also in the future. A manual
request is the probe that runs through a tripped breaker, and a probe that
succeeds clears it.

failure_code.description:
Typed classification of why this call produced no new summary, when it has
one. A summary model call that failed reports its model error code
(`request_failed`, `stream_interrupted`, `rate_limited`, ...); a segment the
runtime refused to send reports its own code
(`compaction_request_unbounded`, see `COMPACTION_REQUEST_UNBOUNDED_CODE`),
which is not a model error at all — the Provider was never called. Never
the provider's message or response body.

mode.description:
Mode of the compaction state the session now holds:
`none`, `deterministic`, `model_generated`, `automatic`, `degraded`, or
`disabled`.

next_attempt_after.description:
When the automatic path may next probe a tripped breaker, as an RFC 3339
timestamp. Present only while it actually refuses something, i.e. while
`circuit_open` is true and this instant is still ahead: read the two
together as "auto compaction is refused until then". Absent means nothing
is being refused — the breaker is not tripped, its window has already
elapsed (so the next automatic attempt may spend the probe), or a window
is armed below the threshold and therefore refuses nothing. A successful
probe clears it, and a failure arms it; the session keeps it across
restarts, so it is the same answer a later request reads.

runtime_run_id.description:
The runtime run whose prompt state was compacted. Absent when the session
has no run yet, in which case there is nothing to compact.

summary.description:
The summary, bounded to [`PRODUCT_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_EXCERPT_CHARS`]
characters. Absent when the session holds no summary.

token_estimate.description:
Token estimate of what the next turn's prompt will carry for this
session, as persisted in its checkpoint.

triggered.description: Whether this call produced a new summary.

ProductSessionId.description: Server-owned product conversation identity, distinct from runtime SessionId.

ProductSessionOutcome.description:
How the most recent finished turn in a session ended.

This is deliberately separate from [`ProductSessionStatus`]: a turn that
produced a final answer, a turn the user cancelled, and a turn that failed
can all leave the session `idle` (or `needs_attention`), so only this records
*how* the last turn ended. `None` means the session has never finished a
turn, which is what keeps "just completed" distinguishable from "never ran".

next_cursor.description:
Token that returns the next page, absent on the last page.

Absent means "no more rows", which is what lets a client stop without
issuing one extra request to discover an empty page.

has_more.description:
Explicit `next_before_ordinal.is_some()` for clients. Present only on a
cursor page, so a legacy request keeps its exact previous body.

next_before_ordinal.description:
Cursor for the next older page: the ordinal of this page's oldest run,
present only on a cursor page while strictly older runs remain.

answer_aborted.description:
Additive R2b projection of this segment's `events`: `true` only when the
segment carries a salvaged partial — an `llm_message` whose `aborted`
marker is `true`, meaning the user stopped the turn after it had already
published text. The field is omitted when it does not apply, so a
response for a run without such a message keeps its previous bytes, and
it never changes the meaning of `run_status`: a stop that produced
nothing and a failed turn both stay unmarked.

`true` is conclusive: it is read off an event this segment actually
carries. Absence is conclusive only when the response reported
`status: "complete"`; a segment inside a `partial` response describes
just the events it projected, and the response's `partial_reasons` say
why it may be short, so a client that needs certainty must read the
response status rather than this field alone.

inherited.description:
True when this segment is a read-only reference inherited at a fork
boundary rather than an event written by the requested product session.

canonical_root.description: Canonical absolute execution root resolved by the server.

ProductWorkspaceId.description: Server-owned identity for one product workspace catalog entry.

PromoteProductMessageRequest.description:
Optional body of a message promotion. An absent body keeps the historical
`current_run` behaviour, so existing callers are unaffected.

pruned_excerpt_bytes.description:
Serialized bytes those messages occupy as the request carries them, so
the elision is measurable rather than implied.

pruned_omitted_bytes.description:
Serialized bytes those messages occupied, and therefore the material the
request did not carry. Recorded beside the count because "three messages"
and "three kilobytes" are different answers to "how much was left out".

pruned_omitted_messages.description:
Older messages left out so the request itself stayed within its byte and
message bounds. Zero when the whole dropped prefix fit.

pruned_payload_bytes.description:
Serialized bytes the pruned messages occupied before the projection, so
`pruned_payload_bytes - pruned_excerpt_bytes` is the whole loss: the
elided payload text, the blocks that repeated it, and the framing.

pruned_payload_digests.description:
Bounded list (newest first, capped by the compaction policy) of
`result id + content digest` for the elided payloads.

pruned_tool_results.description:
How many oversized tool payloads the compaction probe's request elided.

Bounded pruning facts of one turn's shrink request. They are `None`-free
and omitted while zero/empty, so a build that pruned nothing serializes
exactly the bytes it serialized before this field existed.

pruning_policy.description:
Which pruning rule produced the excerpt above, so a trace reader can tell
two policies apart. Absent when nothing was pruned.

next_attempt_after.description:
When the automatic path may next probe a tripped breaker, as an RFC 3339
timestamp.

The breaker is a session fact, so its cooldown has to be one too: the
count is cleared only by a successful summary, and a count that survives
a restart without a deadline would either retry a known-broken model on
every turn or — once seeded — never compact again. `None` means no window
is armed, which an older snapshot also decodes to: a missing deadline is
read as expired, so the worst case of a legacy or corrupt value is one
bounded probe, never a session that can no longer compact itself.

ProviderModelsRequest.description:
Request body for listing models available on a provider endpoint.

Requires a typed provider profile (`provider_type` + `api_base`).
For OpenAI/Anthropic families the API key is read from `api_key_env` on the
server process; Ollama and Fake do not need a key.

models_endpoint.description:
Optional override for the models inventory URL. When omitted the API
uses the protocol default (`{api_base}/models`, Anthropic `/v1/models`,
Ollama `/api/tags`).

ProviderModelsResponse.description: Catalog of model ids returned by a provider inventory endpoint.

name.description:
Optional display label. When empty, the API derives a name from
`api_base` (hostname). Use `provider_type` to select the type, not `name`.

provider_type.description:
User-facing provider type. Values: `openai`, `openai-responses`,
`anthropic`, `ollama`, `fake`. Official and relay endpoints share the
same type; only `api_base` / key / model differ.

ReorderProductMessagesRequest.description:
Atomic successor-queue reorder. The list must name exactly the session's
current queued (pending successor) messages, in the wanted order; a stale or
partial list is rejected instead of being merged, which is what makes a
concurrent promote, revoke, or drain a typed conflict.

ReviewTargetSummary.description:
Secret-free, bounded target projection used by CLI, API, Web, and durable
Review results. Materialized bytes and diff payloads remain in the external
Review snapshot store only.

RiskLevel.description: How risky following the procedure is.

RunModelSnapshot.description:
Secret-free provider/model fact pinned for one run.

This contract lives in Runtime so every shell can persist and compare it
without making Runtime depend on first-party bootstrap configuration.

Sensitivity.description:
How sensitive an artifact's bytes are, which drives retention and whether a
payload may be projected at all.

StepAttempt.description:
Identity persisted while a planned step attempt is in flight.

It deliberately contains no model/tool output.  If a process disappears
after this projection is written, resume can close the attempt as
`interrupted` without replaying an unknown side effect.

StepCompletionBasis.description: Safe explanation for how a step was concluded.

StepRecord.description: Append-only facts for a terminal step attempt.

StepRecordStatus.description: Terminal outcome of one bounded step attempt.

StrategySelectionSource.description: Where the selected strategy came from.

StreamEvent.description:
All events emitted by the engine's streaming main loop.

Consumers (CLI, API/SSE, Web) pattern-match on these to render output.
Adding a new variant forces all consumers to handle it (exhaustive match).

oneOf.description:
A new run has started.

`content_blocks` carries the image content the run's user message
projects (additive, omitted when empty, so every pre-image trace line,
API frame, and snapshot parses unchanged). It rides on the event —
not only in the request — because the trace is what a resume replays:
blocks that live only in the request would silently vanish on resume.
Immutable Agent profile selected before planner/model work begins.
Trusted workspace instruction bundle admitted for this run.
Resolved execution policy selected before planner/model work begins.

A nested workspace instruction became active for a concrete model-turn
target. The body is intentionally absent from the event/trace.
Deterministic procedure selection, by identity only.
A selected procedure body was admitted into the bounded prompt prefix.

A bounded procedure projection was supplied to a concrete execution
boundary. The body is never included; the application fact is enough
for resume, diagnostics, and evidence correlation.

A step explicitly departed from selected procedure guidance. This is a
fact for evaluation, not a permission or approval signal.

Monotonic multidimensional budget projection after a lifecycle phase or
at an exhaustion boundary.

snapshot.description: Boxed to keep the canonical event small; the wire shape is unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Explicit fallback/degradation fact. Safe summaries never contain hidden
reasoning or provider payloads.
A chunk of streaming text from the LLM.
A safe runtime progress note. This must not contain hidden reasoning text.

A model call is being retried under the run loop's recovery budget.

`attempt` is the 1-based index of the attempt that is about to run, so
the first retry is attempt 2, and `max_attempts` is that failure class'
total budget including the first call. `reason` is a whitelisted summary
(`rate_limited` or `transient:<error code>`) and never carries provider
payloads, messages, or secrets.

The LLM finished producing a complete message.

The same variant also carries a salvaged cancelled turn: text the user
had already seen, persisted instead of dropped when a cancel cut the
model turn short. `aborted` is the marker that separates the two facts.

aborted.description:
Set when this message was salvaged from a cancelled turn rather than
delivered as a complete model response. The run's terminal state
stays `cancelled`; a complete message and a cancelled run are
separate facts. Traces written before this field existed are
`false`, which is exactly the pre-salvage meaning.

oneOf.description:
Canonical assistant turn. Older traces omit this additive field
and are reconstructed through the legacy message projection.
A tool call has been requested by the LLM.
A destructive tool call requires explicit approval before it may run.
A tool call completed successfully.
A tool call failed.

A tool payload became a durable artifact.

Carries only the reference. The payload never travels on the event
stream, so a large artifact cannot bloat a trace or an SSE frame.

A tool payload was refused by an artifact quota.

Emitted so a quota event stays visible in the trace and in
diagnostics even though no payload was retained.

block_ordinal.description: Position of the originating content block.

observed_bytes.description: Bytes observed before the read was stopped.

oneOf.description:

StructuredToolContent.description: Structured content a tool returned, with its schema verdict.

schema_valid.description:
Whether a declared output schema was satisfied. `None` when the tool
declared no output schema.

ToolArtifactKind.description: What an artifact holds, as classified locally after validation.

ToolArtifactRef.description:
Reference to a durable artifact. The envelope carries references, never
payload bytes, so a result stays small no matter how large the data was.

mime_type.description:
MIME type as validated locally. `None` when the claim was rejected or
absent; it is never guessed from a filename or from the bytes.

original_uri.description:
URI the remote claimed, retained for provenance only. It is not
resolved, fetched, or used to build a local path.

sha256.description: Hash of the exact retained bytes.

storage_ref.description: Locally generated storage locator. Never a remote-supplied path.

validation_detail.description: Why validation did not pass, when it did not.

ToolArtifactSource.description:
Where an artifact came from. Every field is either locally generated or a
hash, so provenance can be shown and audited without leaking a session
value or a raw remote header.

block_ordinal.description: Position of the originating content block in the tool's result.

ToolCall.description: Normalized tool call emitted by a provider stream.

ToolCallRef.description: A tool call reference recorded on an assistant message for provider replay.

ToolContentBlock.description:
One piece of a tool result.

Binary kinds never carry bytes here: they carry an artifact reference plus
an optional bounded, non-executable preview. `Unknown` exists so a block
type this build does not model is preserved rather than silently dropped.

oneOf.description: A link the remote offered. Recorded, never followed here.

preview.description: Bounded, text-only preview. Absent for sensitive or active content.

oneOf.description:
A block whose declared type this build does not model. The declared
type name and a bounded body are kept so nothing is lost.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Not a message.

ToolError.description: Errors from the runtime-neutral tool execution boundary.

oneOf.description:
The request was well-formed but Runtime-owned context must be applied
before the operation can be reconsidered. No tool dispatch occurred.

ToolErrorDomain.description:
Where an error came from, so diagnostics stay classifiable without parsing
a human-readable message.

ToolOutputEnvelope.description:
The one rich tool result shape.

`summary_text` is the legacy text projection and is always populated, so
every existing consumer keeps working unchanged while richer consumers read
the blocks, structured content, and artifacts.

ToolProtocolMetadata.description:
Display-safe protocol facts about how a result was produced.

Every remote-derived value here is a hash or a locally validated name.
There is deliberately no field for an Authorization header, a raw header
map, or a readable session ID.

attempt_count.description:
How many dispatch attempts produced this result. Zero means the tool
was local and never dispatched over a protocol.

protocol.description: Protocol family, for example `mcp`. Absent for a purely local tool.

oneOf.description:
Rich result detail, when the tool produced one.

Additive and skipped when absent, so an artifact written by an older
build still deserializes and a consumer that only reads `output` and
`metadata` is unaffected. Boxed to keep `ToolResult` small.

ToolResultOutcome.description:
Why a tool result ended the way it did, at the granularity a caller needs
to decide whether retrying is safe.

This is distinct from [`ToolExecutionStatus`], which stays as the coarse
persisted status. `Indeterminate` and `TimedOutKnownNotSent` exist because
a tool call can have external effects: only the latter is safe to retry.

TurnProvenance.description:
Safe provider provenance.  Wire payloads, signatures, and headers remain
private to the provider adapter.

oneOf.description: Omission preserves the current value for C0 clients.

expected_revision.description:
Optional for C0 compatibility. Settings clients send the last observed
revision so concurrent writes fail instead of silently overwriting.

Usage.description: Token usage from a single model call.

WireCallReference.description:
Provider/protocol-bound call identity.  It is never used as a Runtime
approval or artifact identity.

get.description:
The pair is the whole lookup: an attachment that belongs to another session
is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, which is what keeps this
endpoint from confirming another session's identifiers.

There is deliberately no list endpoint in this batch, so a client cannot
enumerate a session it does not own: the upload response is the only way an
attachment id becomes known.

Verification and service are two opens of the same path, so a payload
swapped in between is a real, narrow window rather than an absent one. What
bounds it is the pin: the bytes sent are read from the same path whose length
and digest were just verified, so a swap can only ever yield bytes this
build did not verify and would refuse — a different file that happens to
match the recorded length *and* digest is byte-identical by construction. The
residual is a provenance question (which file the successful open named), not
a content-exposure one, and closing it would mean re-implementing the audited
range and disposition path around an already-open handle instead of reusing
`serve_file`.
